question: Does removing independent per-update weight decay improve the adopted D256 MLA recipe at fixed peak LR0.00125?

architecture_review.candidate: Parallel attention/FFN residual composition with separate branch norms
architecture_review.decision: Deferred distinct topology question; requires explicit branch-input/cache and shared-initialization contracts. Recent local mixing gave a small inconsistent gain; first isolate the previously deferred regularization hypothesis rather than another architecture-plus-LR search.

hp_review.rationale: Existing decay was carried through architecture rounds; its per-step shrinkage is independent of scheduled LR. Isolate whether that regularization helps this short1200-update recipe; neither improved nor worsened quality is assumed.

proposal.backbone: D256 MLA score0.5/SwiGLU672/SiLU/blockRMS/no product norm/no warmup/H200
proposal.scientific_design: After numerical/full-model/worker prerequisites, new seed census, measured complete capacity and resource pilots: prospectively freeze only three fresh paired seeds at common fixed LR. No LR screens or retrospective LR rescue; full six trajectories, inference and original strict quality gates remain required.
proposal.scope: Standard-recipe comparison, not separately optimized best-LR recipes. Equal zero LR-search budgets. Any later tuning is a separate question, not an extension of this panel.

next_action: Generated real HybridOptimizer Muon/AdamW shrinkage/order/serialized-resume checks; then narrow full-model config/checkpoint/H200/cache integration outside frozen sources. No training freeze until real prerequisites and full capacity fit.
